Subject: Evidence request — LLM training & prompt retention policies

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our procurement privacy review I'm gathering a concise evidence pack about how Redwood handles customer inputs to LLM services. Our main asks are: 1) confirmation that FosterHealth data will not be used to train models (or the conditions under which it would be), 2) how you store prompts & responses (retention windows, pseudonymization, access controls), and 3) any SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ artifacts that speak to logging, data isolation, and key management.

If possible, please provide: a short written statement we can include in our DPIA, an inventory of artifacts (reports/diagrams), and a sample of the logs/metadata fields you retain for inference requests (anonymized). We need these for our DPO and InfoSec review by Nov 20.

Thanks — let me know if you need a template.

Best,
Maya Singh
Head of Vendor Risk, FosterHealth

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide what you need. I'm looping in Marissa (Privacy) and Ben (Security) to pull the artifacts and a concise written attestation for your DPIA.

High level answers up front:
- Redwood provides a documented "no-train" option for hosted and dedicated deployments; customer data is excluded from model training by default for customers that opt-out. Where customers do opt in to training, that is explicit, contractually scoped, and logged.
- Prompt/response storage: inference request metadata and ephemeral caches are retained for operational purposes; full prompt/response transcript retention is configurable per-customer and can be set to ephemeral (24–72 hours) or longer based on contract. Access to stored transcripts is auditable and gated by RBAC and KMS-encrypted storage.

Ben and Marissa will follow up with the specific files and the sample anonymized log export. If Nov 20 is a hard deadline we'll prioritize getting the summary + SOC2/SIG extracts to you before then.

— Irene Choi
Director, Trust & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Hi team / Maya — attaching the evidence pack and a short set of answers to the bullets in Maya's original note. See attachments: redwood_SOC2_summary_2026.pdf, sig_matrix_redwood_2026.xlsx, llm_training_exclusion_playbook_v1.pdf, kv_cache_dataflow_diagram.png. Below are the actionable details you can paste into a DPIA.

1) Training on customer data
- Default: No-train by default for hosted & dedicated customers unless explicit opt-in. Opt-in is recorded in contract/account configuration and requires product team approval.
- Proof artifacts: training_exclusion_playbook_v1.pdf (process + audit steps), and a sliced report showing account-level "train_consent" flags (we can provide a redacted export).

2) Prompt & response retention
- Storage layers: (a) Inference ephemeral cache (KV cache) — retained in memory for low-latency and persisted to encrypted blob storage for warm-starts (default retention 24 hours); (b) Request logs & telemetry — retained in encrypted log store (default 90 days) for observability and billing.
- Controls: retention configurable per-customer via account settings; customers can request strict ephemeral mode (24h) or full deletion on demand. All stored transcripts are encrypted at rest (KMS) and access is restricted to a small set of service roles with MFA and just-in-time privileges.

3) Auditability & non-training evidence
- We keep immutable audit logs of: access to stored transcripts, train_consent changes, export requests, and retention policy updates.
- Attachments include a sample anonymized metadata export (fields: request_id, timestamp, model_variant, token_count, train_consent_flag, region, requester_service_id). Full transcript fields are omitted from the sample for privacy.

4) Security artifacts
- SOC 2 summary and relevant control mapping included. SIG matrix maps our responses to common assessment questions. KMS architecture and key rotation schedule are described in the diagram.

If you want a short one-paragraph attestation we can sign for the DPIA, I can draft it and Marissa will review for legal language.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Applied Security, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_SOC2_summary_2026.pdf; sig_matrix_redwood_2026.xlsx; llm_training_exclusion_playbook_v1.pdf; kv_cache_dataflow_diagram.png

Hi Maya — attaching the short attestation below which you may include in your DPIA. If your DPO needs a signed PDF we can execute that as well.

--- Attestation (draft) ---
Redwood Inference attests that, for FosterHealth accounts configured with "no-train" mode, customer data and prompts are not incorporated into model training pipelines. Retention of prompts and responses is configurable and can be set to ephemeral retention (24 hours) or deleted on request. Access to any stored prompt/response data is restricted, logged, and protected with KMS-managed encryption keys. Changes to training consent or retention settings are audited and can be exported for compliance review.

This attestation is provided for inclusion in customer DPIAs and does not amend contractual terms. For contractual assurances, please reference the executed customer agreement and any addenda concerning data use and training consent.

— Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
